executiveSummary: The week's defining pattern was not any single event but a run of self-corrections: this program surfaced, days late, three separate primary-source-confirmed, consequential developments it had initially missed -- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's 11 Nov resignation amid an FBI-linked counterintelligence inquiry (caught up 23 Nov), the first-ever Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral at APEC Shenzhen on 19 Nov (caught up 24 Nov), and Ukraine's 16-17 Nov strikes on the Kerch Strait/Crimean Bridge and Putin's resulting hardened line (caught up 25 Nov). Once caught up, the Nvidia story itself whiplashed: the board that forced Huang out on 11 Nov reinstated him unanimously on 23 Nov under reported pressure from Trump and Musk, citing no evidence of national-security risk while its own investigation stayed open; Congress's response escalated in three distinct, worsening steps across the week -- a 24 Nov House committees' joint letter demanding White House records, a pledged Jeffries probe of the board and Commerce Secretary Lutnick, and by 27 Nov an explicit Senate Democratic pay-for-access inquiry asking whether ~$26M in Nvidia political contributions influenced the administration's own approval of H200 China chip sales, pulling the White House directly into the matter ahead of a Dec 1-3 hearing calendar that now carries three separate, higher-stakes questions. A second major thread turned concrete: the Senate Appropriations Committee's FY27 defense draft cut Golden Dome's $17.5B request by roughly 46% to ~$9.4B and moved to bar new sole-source contracts above $100M on two SpaceX-linked programs worth ~$6.45B -- the clearest test yet of this program's 6 Sep forecast that Golden Dome award tempo would accelerate, and one the draft currently contradicts, though it remains unenacted. On Iran, the Bahrain-specific axis of the Hormuz campaign extended its pause to roughly ten days with no fourth strike and no CENTCOM reversal of the 17 Nov Sheikh Isa claim, while the broader Hormuz mine-claim campaign moved in the opposite direction -- Iran claimed a second through seventh tanker/LNG-carrier mine strike across the week (24-26 Nov) with zero CENTCOM engagement, and a named independent commercial analytics firm (Orbital Risk Intelligence) stated publicly it finds no supporting evidence for the pattern, a sharper and more attributable form of skepticism than this program could previously cite. China's narrower gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard-materials export suspension, due to lapse on its one-year anniversary (27 Nov), was instead reported extended to 27 Jan 2027 -- a second consecutive rollover reinforcing that the relief pattern tracks the broader US-China trade truce, though no primary MOFCOM text has yet confirmed it even on the expiry date itself. The cyber-exploitation wave widened into new categories (industrial controllers, virtualization orchestration, a Cisco Expressway edge flaw) before pausing for the first multi-day stretch in weeks, with the zero-named-DIB-victim pattern now over two months old and unbroken. Taiwan's local elections, Golden Dome, and the CMMC/CR/ITAR regulatory calendar all head into next week as open, unresolved tests rather than closed questions.
whatChanged: Nvidia's leadership whiplashed twice in 12 days: Jensen Huang resigned 11 Nov amid a board inquiry into an alleged foreign-intelligence approach, then was unanimously reinstated 23 Nov under reported political pressure while the board's own investigation stayed open -- and by 27 Nov, Congress's response escalated from reinstatement-process scrutiny (a 24 Nov House document-request letter) to an explicit Senate Democratic allegation that ~$26M in Nvidia political contributions influenced the administration's own H200 China-export approval.

This program corrected three separate multi-day gaps in its own coverage this week -- the Nvidia resignation, the 19 Nov Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen trilateral (a first-ever three-way leader meeting that produced only a thin 'peace declaration'), and Ukraine's 16-17 Nov Kerch Bridge strikes -- a pattern of missed primary-source events, not three unrelated misses.

The Senate Appropriations Committee's FY27 defense draft cut the Golden Dome request from $17.5B to ~$9.4B (~46%) and would bar new sole-source contracts above $100M on two SpaceX-linked programs (SB-AMTI, Space Data Network) worth ~$6.45B combined, directly testing and currently contradicting this program's standing Golden Dome-acceleration forecast; the draft is unenacted, pending Senate floor action and House conference.

Putin ruled out any Black Sea shipping or energy-infrastructure truce and threatened a 'far more painful' response after the Kerch Bridge strikes, directly undercutting Kushner's 19 Nov claim that Russia had agreed to a 'broader' US-Russia-Ukraine-Europe negotiating format -- a contradiction this program could not reconcile until it identified the intervening bridge-strike event.

Iran's Bahrain-specific strike axis (last claim 17 Nov) extended its pause to roughly ten days, while the broader Hormuz mine-claim campaign accelerated sharply: a third tanker-mine claim (24 Nov), a fourth and fifth (24-25 Nov), and a sixth and seventh (~26 Nov, including a 2M+-barrel supertanker) landed with zero CENTCOM claim-specific response; a named independent firm, Orbital Risk Intelligence, publicly stated (20 Nov, newly surfaced this cycle) it finds no evidence for the pattern.

China's gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard-materials export suspension, whose one-year term expired 27 Nov, was reported by multiple trade-press outlets (not yet a primary MOFCOM text) extended to a new window through 27 Jan 2027 -- a second consecutive rollover.

CISA's KEV catalog widened into new target categories this week (Cisco Expressway edge/collaboration infrastructure, Danfoss industrial controllers, Vates Xen Orchestra virtualization) with 15 additions across three alerts (23-25 Nov), then paused for the first multi-day stretch in several weeks; the zero-named-DIB-victim pattern across all 18+ tracked CVE families passed the two-month mark unbroken.

Nine-plus standing forecasts resolved this week: three CORRECT (Nvidia's permanent-CEO naming via reinstatement, the reinstatement-inquiry forecast resolving within one day, Anthropic's first-week close above its IPO price) and several lapsed-INCORRECT clean-ups (Vulcan's Space-Force-review forecast, the Cisco ISE/Secure Email Gateway and GitLab downstream-compromise victim forecasts), continuing this program's pattern of grading lapsed forecasts honestly rather than leaving them open indefinitely.

trendsEmerging.trend: This program's own collection has a demonstrated blind spot for head-of-state-level and primary-source-filed corporate events when daily attention is captured by a single dominant storyline.
trendsEmerging.evidence: Three consecutive multi-day gaps corrected in three consecutive cycles (23, 24, 25 Nov) -- Nvidia's resignation, the Shenzhen trilateral, and the Kerch Bridge strikes -- all occurred while coverage was concentrated on Anthropic's IPO and then on Nvidia itself.
trendsEmerging.soWhat: Treat any single quiet cycle from this program as inconclusive, not confirmatory; the self-correction mechanism is working, but the underlying collection gap it is correcting for has not been institutionally fixed.

trendsEmerging.trend: Congressional AI-vendor oversight is escalating in category, not just intensity -- from a governance dispute to an alleged integrity failure in the export-control system itself.
trendsEmerging.evidence: The week moved from criticism of a board decision (23 Nov) to a document-seeking letter about that decision (24 Nov) to an explicit pay-for-access allegation reaching the White House and Commerce Secretary Lutnick (27 Nov), with three now-parallel inquiry tracks converging on the same Dec 1-3 hearing window.
trendsEmerging.soWhat: Any AI/GPU compute-vendor risk assessment should track the counterintelligence, process-oversight, and alleged-influence tracks as independently resolving, since a finding on one does not resolve the others.

trendsEmerging.trend: Claim volume and verification are diverging further on the Hormuz campaign, now reinforced by a named independent commercial voice rather than resting solely on CENTCOM's silence.
trendsEmerging.evidence: Seven Iranian mine-strike claims have accumulated since 17 Nov with zero CENTCOM claim-specific engagement; Orbital Risk Intelligence's 20 Nov no-evidence assessment, surfaced this cycle, is the first attributable independent skepticism this program has been able to cite on this specific claim pattern.
trendsEmerging.soWhat: Do not read claim volume as a proxy for actual escalation; watch for either a CENTCOM engagement or a confirmed incident that would resolve the credibility gap in either direction.

trendsEmerging.trend: Legislative scrutiny of concentrated single-contractor positions in space/defense-tech is now producing specific, numbered funding and contracting restrictions rather than general criticism.
trendsEmerging.evidence: The Senate Appropriations Committee's Golden Dome draft names SpaceX specifically, cites a precise dollar exposure (~$6.45B), and pairs a ~46% funding cut with a sole-source contracting bar and a mandated independent cost estimate -- a materially more concrete legislative instrument than this thread has previously carried.
trendsEmerging.soWhat: Track House conference treatment of Section 8127 as the next concrete test of whether this becomes enacted policy or is softened for a presidential priority program.

gotWorse: Golden Dome's funding and contracting-structure risk moved from a schedule/cost-dispute concern to a live, numbered legislative threat: a ~46% Senate committee funding cut and a direct sole-source restriction on SpaceX's two largest related awards.

Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia widened from a corporate-governance dispute into an explicit allegation that political money influenced a national-security-relevant export-control decision, now implicating the White House and a cabinet secretary.

The Ukraine diplomatic track hardened rather than progressed: Russia ruled out the Black Sea/energy truces it had reportedly been weighing and threatens a 'far more painful' response, directly undercutting a separately claimed negotiating-format breakthrough.
The volume of unanswered Iranian Hormuz mine-strike claims roughly doubled this week (three to seven since 17 Nov) with CENTCOM's engagement level unchanged at zero.
gotBetter: China's gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard-materials suspension was reported extended for a second consecutive term (through 27 Jan 2027) rather than allowed to lapse, continuing to ease a near-term materials-supply risk tracked since September, even without primary-source confirmation yet.

Anthropic's ANT shares closed their disclosed first week of trading well above the $83 IPO price, resolving this program's standing forecast CORRECT and removing one open question from the AI-sector risk picture.

The Iran-Bahrain-specific strike axis extended its quiet period to roughly ten days, the longest pause of the current run, even though this program continues to treat it as inconclusive given the campaign's documented reporting-lag history.

A named independent commercial analytics firm's explicit skepticism toward Iran's mine-claim pattern gives this program a more citable, attributable basis for discounting unverified claims going forward, regardless of how the underlying campaign resolves.
newsCycleMissed: The structural significance of Nvidia's leadership whiplash is being covered as a personality/political-pressure story; the more consequential frame -- that the underlying counterintelligence and export-control questions remain fully open regardless of who holds the CEO title -- received less emphasis than the reinstatement drama itself.

The Golden Dome funding cut and SpaceX sole-source restriction is being covered primarily as a budget story; its potential to reshape competitive dynamics for non-SpaceX primes and satellite providers, if the restriction survives conference, received comparatively little forward-looking analysis.

Orbital Risk Intelligence's named, affirmative no-evidence finding on Iran's mine claims is a qualitatively different and more citable form of skepticism than the CENTCOM-silence-based doubt this program has relied on for months, yet it has circulated mainly as a single aggregated data point rather than as the structurally important development it represents for assessing the whole claim pattern.

assumptionsChanged.now: The CEO question resolved by reinstating the ousted CEO himself, while the oversight question expanded into a materially more serious pay-for-access allegation reaching the administration.
assumptionsChanged.implication: Do not conflate the settled leadership-title question with the still-open national-security and export-control-integrity questions; track all three congressional tracks independently through the Dec 1-3 hearings.

assumptionsChanged.was: Golden Dome's near-term trajectory was framed primarily around launch-capacity risk (the Vulcan failure) layered on an unresolved cost dispute, with acceleration still the base case per this program's 6 Sep forecast.
assumptionsChanged.now: A Senate committee has drafted a concrete, numbered funding cut and a direct contracting-structure restriction on the program's dominant contractor.
assumptionsChanged.implication: Treat Golden Dome's funding and contracting trajectory as a live legislative fight through House conference, not a presumption of continued acceleration.

assumptionsChanged.was: The Kushner-Putin tension flagged last week (a claimed 'broader negotiating format' vs. Putin's 'no prospect of immediate talks') appeared to be two officials describing the same situation differently.
assumptionsChanged.now: An intervening event -- the Kerch Bridge strikes -- better explains the divergence: Putin's hardened line followed a specific escalatory strike this program had not yet identified.
assumptionsChanged.implication: When two credible sources describe the same situation in contradictory terms, check first for an unidentified intervening event before assuming simple disagreement.
